Senses.Explanation: The first day opens the year's blessing. Liao'an Qingyu, Huiyue Xu, and Yushan Shangsi use the formula at New Year, commonly completing it with 'all things are renewed' before extending or questioning the seasonal greeting. Liao'an turns the formula into a short proclamation before willow and plum imagery. Huiyue joins it to stable mountains and rivers and the flourishing of the teaching. Yushan answers the public question about the renewed line with 'the grasses and trees give off light,' then repeats the formula in his address.

Senses.PreferredTarget: The new year opens its auspicious beginning; all things are renewed.

Senses.Note: Feiyin returns it as an answer; Fushi asks whether the staff has become new; other masters continue the seasonal address into their own teaching. The formula is also an ordinary seasonal blessing; the selected sources matter because they make it do Chan work.

Senses.Explanation: The new year opens its auspicious beginning; all things are renewed. In New Year sermons, the paired formula opens a question about what changes and what does not, or serves as a direct answer to the question of new-year Dharma. Six present New Year deployments by Feiyin Tongrong, Fushi, Linye Xi, Xiangya Ting, Shuijian Hai. Yunfu Zhi in J34nB309 also develops the new/old problem. Feiyin returns it as an answer; Fushi asks whether the staff has become new; other masters continue the seasonal address into their own teaching. The formula is also an ordinary seasonal blessing; the selected sources matter because they make it do Chan work.

Senses.Explanation: The conventional count of the inherited old cases, invoked as one bulk body to be dismissed, melted, or settled at a stroke. Zhongfeng Mingben rates even a thousand vines of the seventeen hundred worth less than one laugh as they melt, Liangting Jingting's opening instruction declares the whole store, the seventeen hundred cases, and every old monk's tongue to be lies that yet do not lie, Yushan Shangsi's evening verse credits the store with flowing east while the seventeen hundred shake the western dryness, and Jinian Jingxian's small-assembly verse presses the seventeen hundred into an iron wall until it breaks open into good news. Yuan'an Liao sets his Shending furnace to melt the seventeen hundred rotten vines and five thousand worn scrolls at once with nothing leaking through, Xueyan Zuqin sweeps the seventeen hundred exchanges of host-and-guest and the whole store into one bulk and calls them fox spit, Feiyin Tongrong names the seventeen hundred as worn straw sandals that dull his descendants while he teases Zhaozhou's old footnote, and Tianru Weize strings the seventeen hundred ancestral moves with the treasury and the subtle heart and tosses the string aside to walk the road the buddha never walked.

Entries.SourceTerm: 千人排門，不如一人拔關

Senses.PreferredTarget: A thousand people push at the gate; one person drawing the bolt does more.
Senses.Note: A single effective move opens a way that collective pressure cannot force. The line is an old saying reused in current instruction; it need not mean that only one person may pass.

Senses.Explanation: A thousand people push at the gate; one person drawing the bolt does more. A single effective move opens a way that collective pressure cannot force. The source-backed uses include Tian'an Sheng in J26nB187, Yuan'an Feng in J37nB386, Yuanjie Jingying in J39nB453, and Pufu Zhuo in J40nB493. Each is a current use of the full line. The image keeps its paired structure across the records. The line is an old saying reused in current instruction; it need not mean that only one person may pass.

Senses.Explanation: The crowd hyperbole of the Chan records: a thousand men and ten thousand men named as one uncountable mass, the failing measure for the exceptional one. Zhongfeng Mingben's last admonition drives his heirs past even the place where a thousand men and ten thousand men cannot squeeze in, ruling that too a wanting-to-understand thought, Yuanwu Keqin writes to the young temple-builder that one who suddenly gets it returns in day-gown brocade whom the thousand and ten thousand can only gaze at in envy, never finding where he came from, Fozhao Deguang's summer-entry saying rules that before the fifteenth the thousand and ten thousand cannot hold it and after the fifteenth sky-filling nets hang a hundred thousand layers deep, and Ying'an Tanhua promises the alms-collector Gan that once broken through, the thousand and ten thousand cannot cage him nor call him back. Songyuan Chongyue tells the Yefu assembly that from the ancients on, amid a thousand and ten thousand only one or half a one could be caged, Xuefeng Huikong sends his alms-collector off with the colt whose frost hooves flash like lightning, seen by the thousand and ten thousand as he passes, Wuyi Yuanlai sets his four scrutinies for the Dongyan brothers with one standing amid the thousand and ten thousand, facing no one and turning from no one, and Chaozong Tongren asks the Caoxi hall why, if the ancestor entered extinction, a thousand and ten thousand still come to worship — what.

Senses.Explanation: This military maxim contrasts plentiful rank-and-file with the scarcity of one person capable of command. In Chan records it answers what happens when a sword leaves its scabbard, appraises a staff-bearing answer, and measures whether someone can carry a demanding encounter. Xuedou Zong answers the question about the sword after it leaves its scabbard with the maxim; Cuifeng Xian appraises Zhimen's staff that lifts sun and moon with the same contrast. Juelang Daosheng uses the line both when challenged about breaking his wish-granting staff and when speaking of meeting illness directly; Baichi Xingyuan places it after asking what to do with a person of the highest capacity, while Shengke Deyu contrasts the rare general with dead fire and cold ashes.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 昭覺勤舉雪竇頌畢云
ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ：我名慧然。山大笑。昭覺勤舉雪竇頌畢云：者箇笑千古萬古清風凜凜地，為甚麼雪竇却道祇應千古動悲風？也是死而不弔。徑山杲云：兩箇藏身露影漢，殊不顧旁觀者哂。愚菴盂云：仰山向虗空裏穵縫
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1297.xml). Grove of the Mirror of the School (宗鑑法林). Speaker: Yuanwu Keqin (昭覺勤), who raises Xuedou Chongxian's verse and asks why it ends with the phrase.

Senses.Explanation: To “stir a sorrowful wind through a thousand ages” is to leave a verse or exchange with an enduring sorrowful after-effect. In the Blue Cliff Record, Xuedou Chongxian's verse ending the Sansheng–Yangshan exchange uses the line. The Classified Anthology has Shushan Ru use it in a different verse after describing a verbal exchange as having fallen. Grove of the Mirror of the School records Yuanwu Keqin asking why Xuedou uses it. Jieweizhou voices it for the continuing grief of Qu Yuan at the Dragon Boat festival; Baiyu applies it in his own verse on Daoxin. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: A model for a thousand ages is a durable example held up for present practice. Zhean cites austere elders as exemplars, Yulin commends the Guiyang pair, and Lanshi praises a monastic workers service in a funeral address. Senses.Explanation: For people to see through age after age closes Xuedou's verse on the seamless monument. Chan records carry the line from verse commentary into hall acts where masters draw or point out the rounded, tiered image and leave it visibly before their assemblies. Xuedou Chongxian supplies the line in the Blue Cliff Record verse and Yuanwu comments on it. Poshan draws a circle with his staff and recites the tiered-shadow couplet; Zishui draws with his staff before the line; Jiqi answers his question about the underlying text with the same duration claim.

Entries.SourceTerm: 千尺絲綸直下垂，一波纔動萬波隨

Senses.PreferredTarget: A thousand-foot fishing line drops straight; one ripple moves and ten thousand follow
AlternateTargets: A thousand-foot line hangs down; one wave stirs and myriad waves follow
SearchAliases: a thousand foot fishing line one ripple ten thousand waves
Senses.Note: The first line of Boatman Decheng?s fishing verse lowers a very long line into the water; the next shows one ripple setting many others in motion. Later masters use the image to test response to a single move: Tian-an strikes his staff, Jieshi asks how the audience will meet the line, and two commentators weigh the bait and catch in the older verse. The verse does not promise an effortless catch.

Senses.Explanation: "A thousand-foot fishing line drops straight; one ripple moves and ten thousand follow" pictures a move that sets responses in motion. Chan masters use the boatman?s verse to question how a listener meets that move. Tian-an strikes his staff as the first ripple; Jieshi asks how his hearers will respond to the line. Yuanwu appraises the older verse and its critiques; Liao-an points from the bait toward what might actually be caught.

Senses.Explanation: A thousand mountain ridges end at the great peak; ten thousand streams lose their roar in the sea. Use convergence of many paths as an answer about source or completion. Fushi Tongxian and Xiangya Xingting use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Shiqi Tongyun, Xiuye Minglin, and Yanju Deshen give further current deployments. The geological image is a Chan way of pointing, not a map of actual watersheds.

Senses.PreferredTarget: A thousand peaks lean toward the mountain and come to rest; ten thousand streams sound their way to the sea and fade.
AlternateTargets: The peaks bow and settle by the great mountain; the many waters fall silent where they meet the sea.

peaks settle mountain streams fall silent sea Zen
Senses.Note: Wanru raises his whisk and offers the pair after saying he will make the matter plain. Yinyuan answers his own question about the one transmitted matter with it. Heyi strikes his staff and shouts before giving it as his answer to what is fundamental. Yingning cites the pair as an older saying, then applies it to a sustained account of removing the root of birth and death. The latter is his present interpretation, not his original line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 功夫，不必論時日之遲速以為利鈍。古之上士，或十年五載而後悟者、或有不假年月敏捷如矢者、或一生剋苦而無成者，蓋其根基不同，利鈍非一，果能決志力行，遠近必到。先德云：「佛法無多子，久長難得人。」每當自念有識神以來，身所受身，積骨如山，所飲母乳，如四海水，異類循環，靡不歷盡。幸今得聞斯法，可脫生死，安不努力勤修，甘於放過？今之所忽，後之所迷，恐終不能遇於此日也。無論少壯衰朽，固當勉力行之，般若種子從此發芽，祈繩繩不懈，道可圖焉。十道宜專一十、道宜專一道若專一，則操進必正而無雜亂，是能貫通真際。如《法華》云：「惟此一事實，餘二則非真，終不以小乘，引導於眾生。」佛說種種法，為明一切心，若悟一切心，焉用一切法？禪家令參一句子，秪要打脫鼻孔、徹其底蘊，應知此著為我抽生死根、拔無明楔，一朝撥轉，煩惱即菩提、眾生即諸佛，唯在離心意識參、絕凡聖路學，無理會、無方便，唯存篤志疑究，不被餘見所惑，蕩盡倚依，忽地翻身，不一、不二，名不得、狀不得，故云：「千峰勢倒嶽邊止，萬派聲歸海上消。」然百姓日用斯道不自知者，如魚之在水而不知水、人之在性而不知性。魚若知水，則為神龍，一滴便可興雲吐霧、灌注大千；人若知性，則為至聖，便可度生死、超天地。允執厥中，要明喜怒哀樂之未發即一也、天命之謂性即一也，凡有血氣莫不尊親，故曰：配天即一也、道可道非常道即一也、無我無人即一也。總之，聖教單明道體，除此盡為魔說。然吾斯論悉是言句上支離，畢竟如何是一？居士能敏於一，把將山河大地納向微塵中，佛祖無下口處，道一亦是空拳誑小兒，則山僧退身有分。如是始不負今日一會儼若靈山，話柄葛藤一併按下。幸甚，幸甚。示重南金居士示重南金居士古德云：「大道秪在目前，要且目前難睹，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。」此處悟徹者甚多，錯會者不少。如石火電光，迅馬疾風，作速攀鞍，入手尚且遲了八刻，若欲琢方削圓，則何時得有進趣？是以令公參一句無意味語，如庭前柏樹子，為甚喚作祖師西來意？提起時，如足履懸崖，放身命相似，直下無依倚顧盻，向未舉已前一腳踏穿，心智路絕，驀地打徹，始知全身總在裏許，飯籮邊終不餓煞，開眼處豈教墮塹？若此道個西來意，早已鈍置了也，何處更討千七百則陳年葛藤東扯西拽？但向居士道：「若有佛法，商量亦錯；若無佛法，商量亦錯。」畢竟如何即是？咄！錯！錯！

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 功夫，不必論時日之遲速以為利鈍。古之上士，或十年五載而後悟者、或有不假年月敏捷如矢者、或一生剋苦而無成者，蓋其根基不同，利鈍非一，果能決志力行，遠近必到。先德云：「佛法無多子，久長難得人。」每當自念有識神以來，身所受身，積骨如山，所飲母乳，如四海水，異類循環，靡不歷盡。幸今得聞斯法，可脫生死，安不努力勤修，甘於放過？今之所忽，後之所迷，恐終不能遇於此日也。無論少壯衰朽，固當勉力行之，般若種子從此發芽，祈繩繩不懈，道可圖焉。十道宜專一十、道宜專一道若專一，則操進必正而無雜亂，是能貫通真際。如《法華》云：「惟此一事實，餘二則非真，終不以小乘，引導於眾生。」佛說種種法，為明一切心，若悟一切心，焉用一切法？禪家令參一句子，秪要打脫鼻孔、徹其底蘊，應知此著為我抽生死根、拔無明楔，一朝撥轉，煩惱即菩提、眾生即諸佛，唯在離心意識參、絕凡聖路學，無理會、無方便，唯存篤志疑究，不被餘見所惑，蕩盡倚依，忽地翻身，不一、不二，名不得、狀不得，故云：「千峰勢倒嶽邊止，萬派聲歸海上消。」然百姓日用斯道不自知者，如魚之在水而不知水、人之在性而不知性。魚若知水，則為神龍，一滴便可興雲吐霧、灌注大千；人若知性，則為至聖，便可度生死、超天地。允執厥中，要明喜怒哀樂之未發即一也、天命之謂性即一也，凡有血氣莫不尊親，故曰：配天即一也、道可道非常道即一也、無我無人即一也。總之，聖教單明道體，除此盡為魔說。然吾斯論悉是言句上支離，畢竟如何是一？居士能敏於一，把將山河大地納向微塵中，佛祖無下口處，道一亦是空拳誑小兒，則山僧退身有分。如是始不負今日一會儼若靈山，話柄葛藤一併按下。幸甚，幸甚。示重南金居士示重南金居士古德云：「大道秪在目前，要且目前難睹，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。」此處悟徹者甚多，錯會者不少。如石火電光，迅馬疾風，作速攀鞍，入手尚且遲了八刻，若欲琢方削圓，則何時得有進趣？是以令公參一句無意味語，如庭前柏樹子，為甚喚作祖師西來意？提起時，如足履懸崖，放身命相似，直下無依倚顧盻，向未舉已前一腳踏穿，心智路絕，驀地打徹，始知全身總在裏許，飯籮邊終不餓煞，開眼處豈教墮塹？若此道個西來意，早已鈍置了也，何處更討千七百則陳年葛藤東扯西拽？但向居士道：「若有佛法，商量亦錯；若無佛法，商量亦錯。」畢竟如何即是？咄！錯！錯！

Senses.Explanation: The image gathers many peaks around a mountain and many streams at the sea. Wanru, Yinyuan, and Heyi each voice the pair in a distinct present address after a gesture or question. Yingning cites the line and turns it toward his account of what is revealed when dependent supports fall away.

Senses.Explanation: A thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions names the proliferating variety of words, gates, cases, and appearances. Masters test both errors: being lost in the differences and erasing the distinct uses that must still be handled. Kuoan criticizes treating the patriarchs’ myriad differences as arbitrary and asks how their expedient gates can be digested. Dahui says that knowing the myriad differences are one kind leaves a person exposed to attack from every side. Yunmen says pursuing words and explanations produces myriad differences and only greater distance from the matter. Xueyan pairs myriad differences with being threaded through by one principle.

Occurrences.Kwic: 時傍有僧進云：「某甲欲就中重申一問，未審大師還不吝慈悲否？」師云：「已絡索不少也。」進云：「如何是常在途中，不離家舍？」師云：「蝸牛上壁。」進云：「如何是常在家舍，不離途中？」師云：「盲龜拽磨。」進云：「如何是龜毛兔角？」師云：「薰風水繡紋。」進云：「如何是鐵山當面？」師云：「賺殺闍黎。」僧禮拜，云：「不因此問，幾成錯過。」師云：「切忌妄承當。」壬子秋日，師駐寶安金繩，僧舉《麗中禪師語錄》答學人三問請益，師隨問置答。問云：「如何是父母未生前面目？」師云：「古鏡深埋。」問云：「未有此身前，向甚麼處行履？」師云：「不借陰陽地，飄然獨任真。」進云：「便恁麼時如何？」師云：「千年桃核。」問云：「天地未分時，這箇在什麼處？」答云：「不坐萬年床。」進云：「還假承當也無？」師云：「闍黎近前來，向你道。」僧纔近前，師云：「去！你欠伶利。」藩下田生輝居士問：「頃因石蓮禪師上堂，某甲曾問二語不契，今日已承老和尚慈悲垂示，便祈首座更下一轉語。」師云：「試理問看。」問云：「竿木隨身事若何？」師云：「度水登山得渠力。」進云：「逢場作戲又作麼生？」師云：「放開則法輪大轉，握住則佛祖難容。」源流拈頌南海寶象林慧弓詗禪師源流拈頌卷二書記傳一錄初祖菩提達磨大師。因慧可問：「諸佛法印，可得聞乎？」祖曰：「諸佛法印，匪從人得。」可曰：「我心未寧，乞師安心。」祖曰：「將心來，與汝安。」

Senses.Explanation: A thousand-year peach pit is an old shell paired with the question whether its former kernel—or old person—remains. Xiaoyin Daxin asks what old kernel there is to seek, Wuwen Daocan gives the affirmative line that the old kernel is still inside, and Huigong Kaixiong gives the bare image as an answer about what precedes bodily origin. The records preserve both the inherited affirmation and its reversal.

Senses.Note: Xiaoyin Daxin replies to Huiji's test with a question about searching a thousand-year peach pit for an old kernel. Liangting revoices the pair to warn against talk that multiplies without reaching the matter; Shuzhong sets it among images of recognition. Huigong quotes Xuexuan Daocheng using the same pair and then challenges how that answer lands. The old kernel is the point of the image: the answer cannot be retrieved by prying open a preserved shell.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南，晚得佛照光以為之嗣，北磵簡傳之，至物初觀而得晦機熈公。江南既歸國朝，禪宗尊宿共扶其道者，數公而已。晦機尤以老成為國柱石，隆然繼之，名稱普聞於天下者，則廣智全悟大禪師訢公其人也。公諱大訢，字笑隱，姓陳氏。本九江義門，唐尚書操諸孫，分居南昌。先墓有豫章之木特異，神於相地者占之曰：是當生奇男子為名僧，其道大行，樹枯其徵也。已而果然。師生於至元甲申八月二十七日，生之夕，所居宅地若震動，人為驚異。稍長，入鄉校，頴悟過常兒，書過眼輒成誦。其親𢹂以出游，至佛寺，必瞻拜戀慕不能去。父母知其志，俾從伯氏之為僧於郡城水陸院法雲者九年，雲之徒彰為薙髮受具戒。居八年，學問日廣，知求佛法大意。一山萬公住廬山之開先，即往見焉，時年十七。山一見，留之左右，日夕警誨，歎曰：吾友晦機在百丈，子欲諮決究竟，非見吾友不可。師稟命詣百丈，晦機識其奇偉於眉睫間，即使侍方丈。他日，謂之曰：昔黃龍得旨泐潭，領徒游方，及見慈明，氣索汗下。汝且道過在甚處？語未絕，師抗聲曰：千年桃核裏，覓甚舊時仁？久之，俾掌書記。一日，舉百丈野狐話問之，師擬議，晦機震威一喝，師於是羣疑頓釋，得無礙智。同參苦咨問之，師後有頌云：百丈野狐，野狐百丈，埋著一坑，伏惟尚享。諸方多頌之。晦機一日定中見天門有榜，師名為首，因謂師曰：昔東山祖有言：我不得勤，遠則負慈。明矣！汝善保任乎？晦機遷淨慈，師從之，仍以為書記。晦機說法，文理精詣，嘗謂師曰：昔雪竇真淨及我玅喜以來，內自教乘，傍及儒老子百家之言，深入要眇，故其文言浩乎如川，至之不可禦也。師神觀高邁，音吐如洪鐘，素以博洽聞，至其辯論古今，如指諸掌，執筆書事，文士良史莫或過之。一時名勝如恩斷江、如一谿、茂古林、宣無言，卓有行業，皆與師為忘年交。本中峰居天目山之師子巖，中外信向甚盛，師嘗謁之，語至夜參半，忽大風，崖石欲墮，左右辟易，師危坐如平時，峰亦服其定力矣。而學士大夫如吳興趙文敏公孟頫、巴西鄧康莊公文原、四明袁文清公桷、房山高公彥敬、東陽胡長孺汲仲、錢唐仇遠近仁、延祐進士莆城楊戴仲弘、金華黃溍晉卿，及今翰林待制京兆杜本伯原，前後負時盛名，與師為文學之友者也。晦機著萬一山塔銘，屬師代作，請文敏公書之，公一見大驚異，以為真得古文法。公為杭州僧作顯教院記，亦屬師代之，及成，不易一字，署己名以書。至大辛

Occurrences.Kwic: ，平日裏說宗說教，口巴巴地，卻似一班作家，直待同你仔細盤桓，將古人差別去處較勘將來，未免面青面黃，舌頭打肐𦞂。總因你蒲團上未曾坐得十年二十年，不過在門頭戶腦，依通解會，穿鑿穿鑿，鹵莽承當。謂我于此事已看到十八九了，驢鞍橋作阿爺下頷，轉認轉遠。今日恰好除夕，一歲已周，請諸人各各打筭一回，不得自瞞瞞人，取性亂道。果于五家宗旨差別路頭一一透得，直至不疑之地否？果于三乘十二分教了了分明，如觀掌中菴摩羅果否？果于十二時中把捉得住，應用隨緣，直下不走作否？果于腳根下事說到行到，橫來豎去，不犯絲毫，開眼合眼，盡在這裏否？須具有恁般見地，纔有恁般作略。不是你麤心大膽，強作主宰，逢人打三十棒，筭得佛法的；不是你鼠竊狗偷，弄聰明，鬥智巧，算得佛法的；不是你糢糊影響，書本上看來，一切相似語，算得佛法的。人生好光景不多，轉眼二三十年，便成衰老。道人聚會，共學無為，選佛場開，心空及第。八十公公入場屋，此事不當兒戲，大家相聚喫莖虀，也要知他滋味。」普說。「千年桃核裏，覓甚舊時仁？這一絡索切忌提起，提起嘮嘮叨叨說個不歇，未免播揚家醜。昨日有人從弁山來，得攖寧法姪語錄一卷，絫絫千萬言辯剝到底，祗因他數十年前三峰藏禪師曾將我洞宗家裏事請益雲門先師翁并博山和尚，當時兩個老漢直直截截一總荅他去了，只是不曾下得一個註腳，煩他三峰禪師費心費思著了許多言語，攖寧禪師又不合上他釣鉤相罵，饒汝接嘴攖寧，攖寧總沒來由一肚皮好佛法說在空裏，他好心請益，只合好好對他說，為甚惡發起來，使諸方見了作是非得失商量，是何道理？這老宿所問一一是該問的，如今還有許多人疑著，雲溪不惜口業為你諸人解說一上，以息兩家之爭，省得後來牽牽纏纏疑個不了。寶鏡三昧是洞山親口披宣說向曹山的，雖云從雲巖先師得來，卻不曾刻定個時日云某年月日付授，若確確實實是雲巖一五一十說的，何不列在雲巖章次，卻列在洞山章次？古人師承有據，如雪峰云：『自從先德山石頭以來，傳此秘密法門，不敢沒其所自始。』洞山云：『從雲巖先師得寶鏡三昧。』蓋云此旨得自雲巖，明師承有據也。疑他洞山未悟道先付法，好笑好笑，洞山老漢今日被人捉敗了也。你平日口巴巴地，臨末梢頭還要辨個愚癡齋，胡亂一上。也大奇！也大奇！無情說法不思議。若將耳聽終難會，眼裏聞聲便得知。全是弄鬼眼睛，一總沒有來歷，卻不道果

Occurrences.Kwic: 不生敬仰。我今入因沙舊室中，夏坐九旬，忽有人來問法，汝代我說一切法不生，一切法不滅。言訖，掩室而坐。頌云：白夏時將至，垂慈勉進修。人天不敬仰，歲月自遷流。法法無生滅，頭頭有放收。九旬聊掩室，恩大實難酬。結夏，上堂。雲門云：今月十五入夏也，寒山子作麼生？靈巖道：今月十五入夏也，黑漆桶作麼生？旃檀叢林，旃檀圍繞；師子叢林，師子圍繞。衲僧鼻孔大頭垂，金剛腦後三斤鐵。上堂。空生大覺中，如海一漚發。有漏微塵國，皆依空所生。國土依空生，空依大覺生。大覺無所依，是謂光明藏。眾中忽有道：依文解義，座主家風。東搭西兜，時流趣向。衲僧門下，未見作家。山僧聞與麼道，直得倒頭禮拜。何也？將謂猴白，更有猴黑。啟建聖節，上堂。拈拄杖：崇高不極，廣博無涯。是謂聖中之聖，天中之天。馭三光以照臨，總萬㝢而光宅。無思不服，有感必通。畫拄杖：擘開華嶽連天秀，放出黃河徹底清。上堂：相逢不拈出，舉意便知有。颺下柴爿，賣弄不少。罰錢出院，力盡烏江。山上有鯉魚，井底有蓬塵。千年桃核裏，覓甚舊時仁。上堂：大眾，業不可為，業不可避。不見道，假使百千劫，所作業不忘。世尊有金鎗馬麥之報，迦葉有世世金色之報。只此二報，無起相，無滅相，如風吹水，自然成文。滿，散。上堂：一年三百六十日，惟有此日最吉祥。黃河澄清聖人出，文經武緯開明堂。聖人既出，天下太平。無為而治，不令而行。南北風塵俱蕩盡，熈熈萬姓歌黃唐。上堂：不用低頭思量，難得菩提煩惱。熱椀鳴聲，譬如煉鐵成器，入火則紅，出火則黑，鐵性如故。上堂：圓明了知，不由心念。活活鱍鱍，蓋地蓋天。去却七，三存一。合眼跳黃河，黃昏候日出。端午，上堂。五月五日端午節，競渡江頭歌管咽，衲僧共啜菖蒲茶，無限馨香生頰舌，百病消除，千妖殄滅。文殊令善財採藥，善財拈草度與文殊，石上栽華，文殊接得，示眾云：此藥亦能殺人，亦能活人，空中釘橛。顧視左右，云：莫有與文殊、善財作主底麼？喝一喝。上堂，舉：教中道：凡夫實謂之有，二乘析謂之無，圓覺謂之幻有，菩薩當體即空。拈云：虎咬大蟲，蛇吞鼈鼻。上堂：十五日以前，崖標嶽峙；十五日以後，電激雷奔；正當十五日，風不鳴條，雨不破塊。拈拄杖云：拄杖子！久默斯要，不務速說。茲見人天普集，佛事興隆，剛要出來露箇消息，爭奈落在靈巖手中，要橫不得橫，要豎不得豎。雖然，執之失度，必入

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 南，晚得佛照光以為之嗣，北磵簡傳之，至物初觀而得晦機熈公。江南既歸國朝，禪宗尊宿共扶其道者，數公而已。晦機尤以老成為國柱石，隆然繼之，名稱普聞於天下者，則廣智全悟大禪師訢公其人也。公諱大訢，字笑隱，姓陳氏。本九江義門，唐尚書操諸孫，分居南昌。先墓有豫章之木特異，神於相地者占之曰：是當生奇男子為名僧，其道大行，樹枯其徵也。已而果然。師生於至元甲申八月二十七日，生之夕，所居宅地若震動，人為驚異。稍長，入鄉校，頴悟過常兒，書過眼輒成誦。其親𢹂以出游，至佛寺，必瞻拜戀慕不能去。父母知其志，俾從伯氏之為僧於郡城水陸院法雲者九年，雲之徒彰為薙髮受具戒。居八年，學問日廣，知求佛法大意。一山萬公住廬山之開先，即往見焉，時年十七。山一見，留之左右，日夕警誨，歎曰：吾友晦機在百丈，子欲諮決究竟，非見吾友不可。師稟命詣百丈，晦機識其奇偉於眉睫間，即使侍方丈。他日，謂之曰：昔黃龍得旨泐潭，領徒游方，及見慈明，氣索汗下。汝且道過在甚處？語未絕，師抗聲曰：千年桃核裏，覓甚舊時仁？久之，俾掌書記。一日，舉百丈野狐話問之，師擬議，晦機震威一喝，師於是羣疑頓釋，得無礙智。同參苦咨問之，師後有頌云：百丈野狐，野狐百丈，埋著一坑，伏惟尚享。諸方多頌之。晦機一日定中見天門有榜，師名為首，因謂師曰：昔東山祖有言：我不得勤，遠則負慈。明矣！汝善保任乎？晦機遷淨慈，師從之，仍以為書記。晦機說法，文理精詣，嘗謂師曰：昔雪竇真淨及我玅喜以來，內自教乘，傍及儒老子百家之言，深入要眇，故其文言浩乎如川，至之不可禦也。師神觀高邁，音吐如洪鐘，素以博洽聞，至其辯論古今，如指諸掌，執筆書事，文士良史莫或過之。一時名勝如恩斷江、如一谿、茂古林、宣無言，卓有行業，皆與師為忘年交。本中峰居天目山之師子巖，中外信向甚盛，師嘗謁之，語至夜參半，忽大風，崖石欲墮，左右辟易，師危坐如平時，峰亦服其定力矣。而學士大夫如吳興趙文敏公孟頫、巴西鄧康莊公文原、四明袁文清公桷、房山高公彥敬、東陽胡長孺汲仲、錢唐仇遠近仁、延祐進士莆城楊戴仲弘、金華黃溍晉卿，及今翰林待制京兆杜本伯原，前後負時盛名，與師為文學之友者也。晦機著萬一山塔銘，屬師代作，請文敏公書之，公一見大驚異，以為真得古文法。公為杭州僧作顯教院記，亦屬師代之，及成，不易一字，署己名以書。至大辛

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 不生敬仰。我今入因沙舊室中，夏坐九旬，忽有人來問法，汝代我說一切法不生，一切法不滅。言訖，掩室而坐。頌云：白夏時將至，垂慈勉進修。人天不敬仰，歲月自遷流。法法無生滅，頭頭有放收。九旬聊掩室，恩大實難酬。結夏，上堂。雲門云：今月十五入夏也，寒山子作麼生？靈巖道：今月十五入夏也，黑漆桶作麼生？旃檀叢林，旃檀圍繞；師子叢林，師子圍繞。衲僧鼻孔大頭垂，金剛腦後三斤鐵。上堂。空生大覺中，如海一漚發。有漏微塵國，皆依空所生。國土依空生，空依大覺生。大覺無所依，是謂光明藏。眾中忽有道：依文解義，座主家風。東搭西兜，時流趣向。衲僧門下，未見作家。山僧聞與麼道，直得倒頭禮拜。何也？將謂猴白，更有猴黑。啟建聖節，上堂。拈拄杖：崇高不極，廣博無涯。是謂聖中之聖，天中之天。馭三光以照臨，總萬㝢而光宅。無思不服，有感必通。畫拄杖：擘開華嶽連天秀，放出黃河徹底清。上堂：相逢不拈出，舉意便知有。颺下柴爿，賣弄不少。罰錢出院，力盡烏江。山上有鯉魚，井底有蓬塵。千年桃核裏，覓甚舊時仁。上堂：大眾，業不可為，業不可避。不見道，假使百千劫，所作業不忘。世尊有金鎗馬麥之報，迦葉有世世金色之報。只此二報，無起相，無滅相，如風吹水，自然成文。滿，散。上堂：一年三百六十日，惟有此日最吉祥。黃河澄清聖人出，文經武緯開明堂。聖人既出，天下太平。無為而治，不令而行。南北風塵俱蕩盡，熈熈萬姓歌黃唐。上堂：不用低頭思量，難得菩提煩惱。熱椀鳴聲，譬如煉鐵成器，入火則紅，出火則黑，鐵性如故。上堂：圓明了知，不由心念。活活鱍鱍，蓋地蓋天。去却七，三存一。合眼跳黃河，黃昏候日出。端午，上堂。五月五日端午節，競渡江頭歌管咽，衲僧共啜菖蒲茶，無限馨香生頰舌，百病消除，千妖殄滅。文殊令善財採藥，善財拈草度與文殊，石上栽華，文殊接得，示眾云：此藥亦能殺人，亦能活人，空中釘橛。顧視左右，云：莫有與文殊、善財作主底麼？喝一喝。上堂，舉：教中道：凡夫實謂之有，二乘析謂之無，圓覺謂之幻有，菩薩當體即空。拈云：虎咬大蟲，蛇吞鼈鼻。上堂：十五日以前，崖標嶽峙；十五日以後，電激雷奔；正當十五日，風不鳴條，雨不破塊。拈拄杖云：拄杖子！久默斯要，不務速說。茲見人天普集，佛事興隆，剛要出來露箇消息，爭奈落在靈巖手中，要橫不得橫，要豎不得豎。雖然，執之失度，必入

Senses.Explanation: The couplet joins one moon across a thousand rivers with spring encountered at every household. Longguang Yin gives the line when asked why Pindola's single body can attend offerings throughout the four quarters. Jianlong Yuan answers with it when asked which wheel of teaching he turns at his opening address. In Buhui Fatong's assembly, an unnamed monk offers it after the clouds disperse and the sun stands in the sky; Buhui answers that it is still a matter at the gate.

Senses.Explanation: Not transmitted by a thousand sages marks the ‘upward road’ or matter that no succession of sages can hand over as received information. In interviews it provokes the questioner to ask what that matter is or why it is not transmitted; answers redirect the question toward going, seeing, trusting, or acting for oneself. Later masters also quote the formula in their own addresses, so each occurrence belongs to its immediate utterer rather than to an anonymous traditional voice.

Senses.Explanation: The expression “a thousand leagues share one wind” (千里同風) joins a stated long distance to a shared wind; Chan records preserve it in comments, hall addresses, and an encounter. One encounter explicitly pairs “not recognizing face to face” with “a thousand leagues nevertheless share one wind.” Guishan Zhe says “it may be called a thousand leagues sharing one wind” after comparing Mazu and Jingshan; another address places the line after “one utterance fits the same track.” These are the texts’ own pairings. The entry makes no broader claim beyond those recorded pairings.

Senses.Explanation: Fenyang gives the image of carrying something a thousand miles only to show the old face as his answer for the phrase of the true command. Jinian independently revoices it while commenting on Nanyue and Mazu. Xuefeng Huikong and Songyuan raise the four-turn teaching and each answers it with a distinct present critique. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: Distance doubled to totality, and the masters who grade a wrong turn by it. Xuedou Chongxian answers the monk who leaps from the way-is-near answer to having heard the unheard with the flat verdict that he is a thousand and ten thousand miles off, Shoushan Xingnian warns the assembly that at this point the eye must fix at once or it is a thousand and ten thousand miles off, like watching a horse through a window, Yuanwu Keqin writes to a patron that what the thousand sages secretly transmit stands more than wall-like ten-thousand fathoms, a thousand and ten thousand miles apart, yet the whole earth picked up holds not one dust of it, Chushi Fanqi sets the dharma with nothing to grasp, straightaway nothing-to-do, rest and cease, against one trampling step forward that lands a thousand and ten thousand miles off, and Yulin Tongxiu tells the assembly that where he truly serves them, even a thousand and ten thousand miles away is still counsel at their ear. Qianyan Yuanzhang tells the assembly that at Wuming's place there is only Wuming and no buddha-dharma, so to take the staff and the shout as a matter for discussion is to fall a thousand and ten thousand miles off, Tianyin Yuanxiu raises that saying and doubles the miss, since not discussing them is a thousand and ten thousand miles off too, Yongjue Yuanxian grades shout and staff as already second and third and any how-about-this on top as straight out a thousand and ten thousand miles, Liangting Jingting warns his correspondent that calling the inward quietude cessation-present is at once a thousand and ten thousand miles off, and Jiqi Hongchu sizes up pilgrims from the far provinces who cross a thousand and ten thousand miles and the lake itself and still do not know where the mountain is.

Senses.Explanation: Dayu Shouzhi places flowering fruit trees in fire and waiting for sunrise at dusk after a deliberately disordered number sequence and a warning that careful calculation becomes a verbal fault. Xiaoyin Daxin repeats the same impossible reversals after saying his staff establishes the teaching banner wherever it goes. Tanfang Shouzhong places them after 'mind is Buddha,' 'not mind, not Buddha,' and 'not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.' The pair stops sequential reckoning by presenting the event where ordinary order says it cannot occur.

Senses.Explanation: “Peach red, plum white, rose purple—ask the spring wind and it knows nothing” places visible differences beside a wind that offers no explanation. Biefeng Zhen gives the line after saying that the upward road is not transmitted by the sages. Nanyue Jiqi uses it as a direct answer when an unnamed monk presses him about establishing a house. The line presents the scene and the unanswered question without assigning a hidden meaning to each flower or color.

Entries.SourceTerm: 桃花流水杳然去，別有天地非人間

Senses.PreferredTarget: Peach blossoms drift away on the stream; beyond is another world outside the human realm
SearchAliases: peach blossoms drift away on the stream; beyond is another world outside the human realm
Senses.Note: Li Bai’s couplet sends peach blossoms downstream toward another world beyond the ordinary human one. Guxue voices it after saying his listeners are already in the deep mountains and asking whether they recognize their surroundings. Liangting places it beside a case about a solitary peak, setting a familiar poem against the Chan exchange. Juelang writes the poem while jailed after refusing to alter his earlier writing, making the line a reply from confinement. Weilin voices it at a birthday sermon after asking who the honored person is and what longevity means. These uses shift the image from geography to the situation facing each speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲擁樓臺山樹低，輕鷗兩兩弄柔荑。可堪月挂秋蘆影，歷亂銀河烏夜啼。僧問投子青：「當今年多少？」子云：「月籠丹桂遠，星拱北辰高。」輦路江風暗，官庭野草春。傷心庾開府，老作北朝臣。僧問芙蓉：「如何是曹洞家風？」蓉云：「繩床風雨爛，方丈草前侵。」歲月人間促，煙霞此地多。殷勤竹林寺，更得幾回過。國師三喚侍者。風前彼我寄相思，歷亂琴心祗自知。今夜月明卿有約，只愁行露晚來遲。同安孤峰迥秀，不挂煙蘿，片月橫空，白雲自異。問余何事棲碧山，笑而不荅心自閒。桃花流水杳然去，別有天地非人間。王老師賣身。王孫落魄走天涯，西望長安客路賒。心事滿腔說不得，只今誰是魯朱家。僧問梁山：「如何是和尚家風？」山云：「益陽水急魚行澀，白鹿松高鳥泊難。」亭亭孤月照行舟，寂寂長江萬里流。鄉國不知何處是，雲山漫漫使人愁。僧問梁山：「如何是正法眼？」山云：「南華裏。」僧云：「為甚在南華裏？」山云：「為汝問正法眼。」門徑俯青溪，茆堂古木齊。紅塵飛不到，時有水禽啼。僧問梁山：「如何是從上傳來底事？」山云：「渡水胡僧無膝褲，背駝梵夾不持經。」中庭地白

Occurrences.Kwic: 痛心於三教大聖之道。世無知者，不究天人費隱，輒敢詆訾大聖，為世亂階。故予不惜狂愚之言，扣擊廣大精微之論，以為天下美利，庶不負佛聖示現，欲此道大同天下，使之洋溢覆載。凡有血氣者，莫不相謀此大公無私之道，而各自尊親以高厚，悠久無疆也。曰：有是哉！予今與爾，亦可謂同心斷金矣。戊子冬，因江院王公屢慕師道化，求師語錄，因閱師原道七論，謂不應稱明太祖三字，遂坐師獄中，師不辯。後陳太宰聞，命一吏省師索偈，師援筆書云：「問予何事棲碧山？笑而不答心自閒。桃花流水杳然去，別有天地非人間。」太宰得偈，嘉歎不已。旻昭居士嘗問師安，師見惟談向上事，不及寒暄，故居獄一年，未嘗有一字干王公大人，日於獄中著金剛心經、周易衍義，以明內聖外王之道。成自匡山圓通禮師足，問云：「不因漁父引，爭得見波瀾？某甲到這裏，請問和上，這是甚麼所在？」師曰：「看腳下。」進云：「鑊湯無冷處，和尚憑何立命安身？」師曰：「還要別求麼？」進云：「曹山三墮，和尚即今居那一墮？」師曰：「此中無人到。」進云：「風前吹玉笛，那箇是知音？」師曰：「要他知作麼？」成禮

Occurrences.Kwic: 道：其如幻耳。祖師云：泡幻同無礙，如何不了悟？達法在其中，非今亦非古。師乃起立，召大眾云：這箇豈不是泡幻？喚什麼作無礙？這箇不是無礙，又喚什麼作泡幻？這裏悟去，無邊剎境自他不隔于毫端，十世古今始終不離于當念。如或不然，看他閒甲子，遷到幾時休？剎那如寂靜，百川應倒流。祖信菴主為師祝壽設齋，請上堂。一入信門，便登祖位。且作麼生信？盡十方世界是一人，盡無量百千劫是一壽。以如是壽，壽如是人，不長不短，不減不增。且道人是何人？壽是何壽？還委悉麼？桃花流水杳然去，別有天地非人間。純一監院同陳輝生道友為師慶壽，請上堂。虗度浮生半百年，知非知命總茫然。饑飡渴飲尋常過，笑破虗空嘴半邊。似這般無出豁漢，不辨月之大小、歲之閏餘，凡不收、聖不管，正好貶向無生國裏，直教覔箇出頭地不得，安用為渠𦘕眉指目、攢花簇錦耶？雖然，這漢却有箇長處，解向人道：飯是米做，鍋是鐵鑄。若也不信，試向自己竈門前、口門邊一一檢點去。兩序眾職事耆舊製師子法被，為師慶壽，請上堂。師子叢林，師子圍繞，踞地底踞地，哮吼底哮吼，返擲底返擲，滾毬的滾毬，直得

Senses.Explanation: A poem’s peach blossoms and disappearing stream become a way to point beyond the place being named. Guxue quotes the couplet after asking the assembly to recognize where they are. Liangting pairs it with a solitary-peak case. Juelang writes the poem while imprisoned; Weilin voices the couplet to answer a birthday-sermon question about the person and longevity.
